rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3 and 3 - own field experiment (TDR soil water profiles in a flood-irrigated and a mulched-drip plot, Kailu County, 2016) plus Hydrus-2D simulations calibrated/validated on those measurements. Q2: Section 3.3, Table 5 - simulated drainage at the bottom boundary was 55.8 mm under flood vs 20.4 mm under mulched drip (about 2.7 times); Section 3.4.1, Fig. 5 - cumulative water fluxes at 1.5-4.0 m were 17.6-5.6 cm under flood vs 9.6-2.0 cm under mulched drip; Section 3.4.2, Fig. 6 - infiltration depth reached 400 cm under flood vs 325 cm under drip; model output was checked against measured soil water content in the same plots (Section 3.2, Fig. 4, Table 4). Q4: Section 3.1, Fig. 3 - measured soil water content along the 150 cm profile was lower under mulched drip in the main growth stage (13.1% lower at 100-150 cm); Table 5 - simulated water balance components (irrigation 228 vs 381 mm, evaporation, root uptake, drainage) describe the pathway from reduced applied water to reduced deep flux. Q8: Section 3.4.1 - authors note the simulation period ran only from planting to harvest and that soil water continued to move downward after harvest, so the reported fluxes are end-of-season values only; abstract/conclusions qualify the recharge reduction as 'to some extent'.
rows.notes: The study compares mulched drip irrigation with flood irrigation, so the effect attributed to 'drip' is confounded with plastic film mulch; treated as drip evidence because the comparison does involve replacing flood by drip, but noted. Recharge itself was not measured (water table at 6.1 m, simulated domain 4 m); the recharge result rests on Hydrus-2D fluxes and infiltration depth, with only soil water content validated against TDR data, hence Q3 no (the measurement and model are not independent lines on recharge). Single site, single crop (maize), single season (Q5 no); plots were 86 and 71 ha but observations were a single profile set at each plot centre and the model is a 2D column, so no scheme or regional result (Q6 no). Only validation statistics (MAE, NRMSE, NSE) reported, no dispersion for the flux/recharge result (Q9 no). No required condition stated from own findings (Q7 no).

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3 and 3 - own 2016 field measurements (TDR soil water profiles, auger samples, weather station) in flood and mulched-drip plots and Hydrus-2D runs calibrated on flood data and validated on drip data. Q2: Table 5 - simulated drainage 20.4 mm under mulched drip vs 55.8 mm under flood; Fig. 5 - cumulative fluxes at 1.5-4.0 m roughly 1.8-2.7 times larger under flood; Fig. 6 - infiltration depth 325 cm under drip vs 400 cm under flood; Section 4.2 and Conclusions - authors infer from these results that mulched drip reduced groundwater recharge and threatens the stability of regional groundwater. Q4: Fig. 3 and Section 3.1 - measured soil water content lower under drip in the main growth stage throughout 0-150 cm; Table 5 water balance components (irrigation amount, evaporation, root uptake, drainage) trace the pathway to reduced deep flux. Q8: Section 3.4.1 - simulation period limited to planting-harvest, soil water continues to move after harvest; results qualified as reduction 'to some extent'.
rows.notes: The 'negative implications for regional groundwater stability' in the passage is the authors' inference (Section 4.2) from plot-scale simulated fluxes; no groundwater level data were measured or modelled in this study, and the regional claim is an extrapolation (Q6 no). Technology is mulched drip (drip plus plastic film) versus flood, so the mulch effect is confounded with drip. One site, one crop, one season; model validated only on soil water content, not on recharge; no dispersion measure for the flux results.

notes: Full text appears complete (some duplicated lines from PDF extraction). Study is a single-season, single-site field plus Hydrus-2D modelling comparison of mulched drip irrigation and flood irrigation for maize; groundwater recharge is inferred from simulated deep fluxes and infiltration depth rather than measured.
